subject: PE
title: Lifetime Fitness II
description: An advanced elective physical education course that prepares seniors to stay active for life after high school. Students design and run their own strength, cardiorespiratory, and flexibility programs, learn individual and dual lifetime activities (pickleball/tennis, golf, hiking and orienteering, cycling, swimming, dance), practice stress management and recovery, and finish with a personal adult fitness plan they can use in college or the workplace.
framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards – High School Course 3 (advanced elective); 2009 California Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-HS3-1.1: Combine and apply movement patterns, from simple to complex, in individual and dual lifetime activities (racket sports, golf).
standards.PE-HS3-1.2: Demonstrate proficient movement skills in outdoor and adventure activities (hiking, orienteering, cycling).
standards.PE-HS3-1.3: Demonstrate proficient movement skills in aquatic and rhythmic/dance activities.
standards.PE-HS3-1.4: Analyze and apply biomechanical principles (force, leverage, stability) to improve performance of lifetime activities.
standards.PE-HS3-1.5: Apply offensive and defensive strategies and rules in individual and dual activities.
standards.PE-HS3-2.1: Assess personal fitness levels on the five components of health-related fitness and set goals.
standards.PE-HS3-2.2: Design, implement, and evaluate a personal fitness plan using the FITT principle, progression, overload, and specificity.
standards.PE-HS3-2.3: Meet health-related fitness standards for cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition.
standards.PE-HS3-2.4: Explain and apply safe resistance-training technique and program design, including periodization.
standards.PE-HS3-2.5: Evaluate nutrition, hydration, sleep, and recovery practices that support activity and long-term health.
standards.PE-HS3-2.6: Evaluate community and commercial fitness resources, consumer claims, and costs for lifelong activity.
standards.PE-HS3-3.1: Explain the psychological benefits of physical activity, including stress reduction and improved mood, and use activity to manage stress.
standards.PE-HS3-3.2: Identify and use strategies for intrinsic motivation, self-monitoring, and overcoming barriers to adult physical activity.
standards.PE-HS3-3.3: Demonstrate leadership, cooperation, safety, and respect for others in group and partner activities.
standards.PE-HS3-3.4: Analyze the social and cultural roles of physical activity and how to build activity into adult life (work, family, community).

units.title: Fitness Assessment and Goal Setting
units.big_idea: You can't plan what you haven't measured.

units.title: Resistance Training Program Design
units.big_idea: Safe technique plus progressive overload builds strength for life.

units.title: Cardiorespiratory Endurance: Run, Bike, Swim
units.big_idea: Training the heart and lungs with the right intensity improves health and performance.

units.title: Flexibility, Yoga, and Recovery
units.big_idea: Mobility, rest, and nutrition make training sustainable.

units.title: Semester Reassessment

units.title: Racket Sports: Pickleball and Tennis
units.big_idea: Dual sports combine skill, strategy, and social connection for a lifetime.

units.big_idea: Precision sports reward consistent mechanics and focus.

objectives: Measure the five components of fitness

days.title: Mile run
days.work: Warm up, then run/walk a timed mile; record time and heart rate.

days.title: Strength tests
days.work: Do max 90° push-ups and curl-ups to cadence; record results.

days.title: Flexibility
days.work: Perform sit-and-reach and shoulder stretch tests; record results.

days.title: Body measures
days.work: Measure resting heart rate, waist circumference, and height/weight privately; learn limits of BMI.

days.title: Compare to standards
days.work: Compare results with Healthy Fitness Zone standards and record in a fitness log.

days.title: Calculate zones
days.work: Calculate target heart rate zones with the Karvonen formula; do a 20-minute brisk walk checking pulse every 5 minutes.

days.title: Intervals
days.work: Do jump-rope intervals (30 s on / 30 s off × 10) and record heart rate and RPE.

days.title: Steady state
days.work: Jog or cycle 25 minutes holding 60–70% heart rate reserve.

days.title: Circuit
days.work: Complete a 20-minute bodyweight circuit (squats, lunges, push-ups, planks) and track RPE.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Graph the week's heart-rate data and explain which workouts hit your zone.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Write three SMART goals based on baseline data; do a 30-minute activity of choice.

days.title: Barriers
days.work: List personal barriers (time, cost, motivation) and two strategies each; complete a 25-minute jog.

days.title: Habit tracking
days.work: Set up a weekly habit tracker; do a Darebee 30-minute full-body workout.

days.title: Activity sampler
days.work: Try a new activity (rock climbing gym, swim, spin class video) for 30 minutes.

days.title: Goal check
days.work: Share goals with a parent and sign a fitness contract.

objectives: Perform foundational lifts with safe technique

days.title: Movement patterns
days.work: Learn the six patterns (squat, hinge, push, pull, carry, lunge) with a broomstick; film form.

days.title: Lower body
days.work: Practice goblet squats and Romanian deadlifts, 3×10, focusing on neutral spine.

days.title: Upper body
days.work: Practice push-ups, band rows, and overhead press, 3×10 each.

days.title: Leverage
days.work: Learn how lever length and joint angle change difficulty; test incline vs. decline push-ups.

days.title: Form check
days.work: Review form video with a checklist and correct two faults.

objectives: Choose reps and load for strength vs. endurance

days.title: Find working loads
days.work: Estimate 10-rep max for five lifts and record loads.

days.title: Strength day
days.work: Do 4×5 of squat and press at heavier load with 2-minute rests.

days.title: Endurance day
days.work: Do 3×15 of lunges, rows, and push-ups with 45-second rests.

days.title: Core
days.work: Do a core circuit (planks, dead bugs, bird-dogs, side planks) × 3 rounds.

days.title: Log review
days.work: Calculate weekly training volume and plan next week's overload.

objectives: Write a 4-week program using FITT and overload

days.title: Program design
days.work: Write a 4-week full-body program (3 days/week) with exercises, sets, reps, and progression.

days.title: Workout A
days.work: Complete Workout A of your program and log it.

days.title: Active recovery
days.work: Do a 30-minute walk and mobility routine.

days.title: Workout B
days.work: Complete Workout B and log it.

days.title: Workout A
days.work: Complete Workout A with progression and note RPE.

days.title: Workout B
days.work: Complete Workout B with added load or reps.

days.title: Cardio
days.work: Do 25 minutes of moderate cardio of choice.

days.title: Workout A
days.work: Complete Workout A with progression.

days.title: Mobility
days.work: Do a 30-minute mobility and foam-rolling session.

days.title: Workout B
days.work: Complete Workout B and review progress.

days.title: Deload
days.work: Do a light deload session at 60% of usual load.

days.title: Retest strength
days.work: Retest 10-rep maxes and push-up/curl-up scores.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Calculate percent improvement and write what worked.

days.title: Teach a lift
days.work: Teach a family member one lift with correct cues.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Take a written quiz on training principles and safety.

days.title: Energy systems
days.work: Learn aerobic vs. anaerobic systems; do an easy 25-minute run.

days.title: Intervals
days.work: Do 6 × 400 m intervals with 90-second recoveries.

days.title: Cross-train
days.work: Do 30 minutes of cycling or swimming.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Run 20 minutes at comfortably hard tempo pace.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Write a 5K training plan for the next 4 weeks.

objectives: Follow and log an endurance plan

days.title: Easy run
days.work: Run 25–30 minutes easy and log pace and heart rate.

days.title: Strength
days.work: Do a runner's strength circuit (single-leg squats, calf raises, glute bridges).

days.title: Fartlek
days.work: Do a 30-minute fartlek run with 8 surges.

days.title: Mobility
days.work: Complete a 30-minute yoga flow for runners.

days.title: Long run
days.work: Run or run/walk 35–40 minutes at easy pace.

objectives: Improve technique in a second endurance activity
materials: public pool access or bicycle and helmet

days.title: Technique
days.work: Swim: practice freestyle breathing and kicks for 30 minutes; or Bike: practice shifting and braking drills in a safe lot.

days.title: Endurance
days.work: Swim 20 continuous minutes or ride 45 minutes on a bike path.

days.title: Run
days.work: Do a 30-minute run with 4 hill repeats.

days.title: Safety
days.work: Learn California bike laws (helmet under 18, lights, lane use) or water-safety rescue skills; do a 30-minute session.

days.title: Intervals
days.work: Swim 8 × 50 m or bike 6 × 2-minute hard efforts.

days.title: Race pace
days.work: Run 3 × 1 km at goal race pace.

days.title: Easy
days.work: Run 20 minutes easy plus strides.

days.title: Cross-train
days.work: Do 30 minutes of easy swimming or cycling.

days.title: Race prep
days.work: Plan race-day nutrition, gear, and warm-up; do a 15-minute shakeout.

days.title: Rest
days.work: Do a light mobility routine and visualization.

days.title: 5K
days.work: Run a timed 5K (local race or measured course) and record splits.

days.title: Recovery
days.work: Walk 30 minutes and stretch.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Compare 5K time to predicted time from your mile test; analyze pacing.

days.title: Strength
days.work: Complete a full-body strength session.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Take a quiz on aerobic training principles.

objectives: Distinguish static, dynamic, and PNF stretching

days.title: Dynamic warm-up
days.work: Learn and perform a 10-minute dynamic warm-up, then jog 20 minutes.

days.title: Static stretching
days.work: Perform a 30-minute static stretching routine holding each stretch 30 seconds.

days.title: PNF
days.work: Practice PNF hamstring and chest stretches with a partner or strap.

days.title: Mobility
days.work: Do a hip and shoulder mobility routine.

days.title: Retest
days.work: Retest sit-and-reach and shoulder stretch; compare with baseline.

objectives: Use yoga and breathing to manage stress

days.title: Breathing
days.work: Practice box breathing and 4-7-8 breathing; do a 20-minute walk.

days.title: Yoga flow
days.work: Follow a 30-minute vinyasa yoga video.

days.title: Stress and exercise
days.work: Read about exercise and mental health; log mood before and after a 30-minute workout.

days.title: Balance poses
days.work: Practice balance poses (tree, warrior III, half moon) for 30 minutes.

days.title: Restorative
days.work: Do a 30-minute restorative yoga and body-scan meditation.

days.title: Food log
days.work: Log your food for three days; do a 30-minute workout of choice.

days.title: Fueling
days.work: Learn pre- and post-workout fueling; plan a sample day of meals.

days.title: Hydration
days.work: Calculate sweat loss by weighing before and after a 30-minute run.

days.title: Sleep
days.work: Track sleep for the week and write a sleep-hygiene plan.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Write an evaluation of your nutrition, hydration, and sleep with two changes.

days.title: Mile retest
days.work: Retest the mile run.

days.title: Strength retest
days.work: Retest push-ups and curl-ups.

days.title: Flexibility retest
days.work: Retest flexibility and resting heart rate.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Graph baseline vs. current scores.

days.title: Goal review
days.work: Review SMART goals and mark each as met or not.

objectives: Revise the fitness plan for semester 2

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on your semester training and what motivated you; do a 30-minute workout.

days.title: New goals
days.work: Write new SMART goals for semester 2.

days.title: Revise plan
days.work: Revise your weekly plan to include strength, cardio, and a lifetime sport.

days.title: Choice workout
days.work: Lead a family member through a workout you designed.

days.title: Written exam
days.work: Take the semester written exam on fitness concepts.

objectives: Perform serve, return, dink, and volley
materials: public court or driveway with tape lines

days.title: Rules and serve
days.work: Learn rules and scoring; practice underhand serves (20 per side).

days.title: Dinks
days.work: Practice dinking at the kitchen line with a partner for 20 minutes.

days.title: Volleys
days.work: Practice volleys and blocks; play a short game.

days.title: Third-shot drop
days.work: Practice third-shot drops and play doubles.

days.title: Skill check
days.work: Complete a skill test (serves in, dink rally length) and play a game.

days.title: Positioning
days.work: Learn doubles positioning and communication; drill transition-zone movement.

days.title: Game play
days.work: Play doubles games, tracking unforced errors.

days.title: Community play
days.work: Attend open play at a local park or recreation center.

days.title: Fitness
days.work: Do agility ladder and lateral shuffle drills for court movement.

days.title: Tournament
days.work: Play a family round-robin tournament demonstrating etiquette and scoring.

days.title: Forehand
days.work: Practice forehand grip and swing; hit 50 balls against a wall.

days.title: Backhand
days.work: Practice one- or two-handed backhand against a wall.

days.title: Serve
days.work: Practice the serve motion using kinetic chain cues.

days.title: Rally
days.work: Rally with a partner, counting consecutive shots.

days.title: Scoring
days.work: Learn tennis scoring and play mini-tennis games.

objectives: Play singles and doubles with strategy

days.title: Net play
days.work: Practice volleys and approach shots.

days.title: Singles
days.work: Play a singles set.

days.title: Doubles
days.work: Play doubles focusing on positioning.

days.title: Film review
days.work: Film your forehand and compare with a pro's slow-motion swing.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Take a racket-sports rules and strategy quiz and play a match.

objectives: Perform putting, chipping, and full swing

days.title: Putting
days.work: Practice putting from 3, 6, and 10 feet; record make percentage.

days.title: Chipping
days.work: Practice chipping to a target from 10–20 yards.

days.title: Full swing
days.work: Learn grip, stance, and full swing at a driving range (one small bucket).

days.title: Biomechanics
days.work: Analyze how leverage and rotation produce club-head speed.

days.title: Skill check
days.work: Complete a putting and chipping skills test.

objectives: Play a short course with etiquette

days.title: Pre-shot routine
days.work: Develop a pre-shot routine and practice at the range.

days.title: Etiquette
days.work: Learn course etiquette and rules; practice putting.

days.title: Course play
days.work: Play 9 holes at a pitch-and-putt course and keep score.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Analyze your scorecard for strengths and weaknesses.

days.title: Fitness
days.work: Do a rotational core and mobility workout for golf.

days.title: Ten Essentials
days.work: Pack the Ten Essentials and learn Leave No Trace principles.

days.title: Conditioning
days.work: Do stair or hill repeats with a loaded daypack for 30 minutes.

days.title: Plan a hike
days.work: Plan a 4–6 mile hike in a local or state park, including weather, elevation, and emergency plan.

days.title: Hike
days.work: Complete the planned hike with a family member, logging time and heart rate.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a trip report with distance, elevation gain, and lessons learned.

days.title: Topo maps
days.work: Read contour lines on a USGS topo map and identify hills, valleys, and saddles.

days.title: Compass
days.work: Learn to take and follow a bearing; adjust for declination.

days.title: Backyard course
days.work: Set up and complete a 5-point backyard or park orienteering course.

days.title: Park course
days.work: Complete a permanent orienteering course or geocaching route in a local park.

days.title: Skill check
days.work: Pass a navigation skills test.

objectives: Ride safely and plan a route

days.title: Maintenance
days.work: Learn the ABC check (air, brakes, chain) and fix a flat tire.

days.title: Route
days.work: Plan a safe 10–15 mile route using bike lanes or trails.

days.title: Ride
days.work: Complete the ride, logging time, distance, and heart rate.

days.title: Commute
days.work: Plan a bike or walk route to a future job or campus and time it.

days.title: Strength
days.work: Complete a full-body strength workout.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan an outdoor outing for family or friends (hike, bike, kayak) with a risk-management plan.

days.title: Conditioning
days.work: Do a 40-minute conditioning session.

days.title: Lead outing
days.work: Lead the outing, briefing safety and Leave No Trace.

days.title: Debrief
days.work: Debrief participants and record feedback.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Take an outdoor-safety quiz and write about how outdoor activity fits your adult life.

objectives: Perform basic steps from several dance forms

days.title: Cumbia
days.work: Learn basic cumbia steps and their cultural origins; dance for 30 minutes.

days.title: Swing
days.work: Learn East Coast swing basic and a turn with a partner.

days.title: Line dance
days.work: Learn two line dances.

days.title: Heart rate
days.work: Dance continuously for 30 minutes, tracking heart rate.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Perform a dance for family and explain its cultural background.

days.title: Counts
days.work: Learn to count music in 8s and follow a 30-minute dance fitness video.

days.title: Choreograph
days.work: Choreograph a 3-minute dance fitness routine.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse and refine the routine.

days.title: Teach
days.work: Teach the routine to family members.

days.title: Record
days.work: Record the routine and reflect on fitness benefits.

objectives: Evaluate gyms, apps, and products as a consumer

days.title: Gym options
days.work: Compare costs and contracts of three gyms, a community center, and free options; do a workout.

days.title: Apps and wearables
days.work: Evaluate two fitness apps and a wearable for usefulness and privacy.

days.title: Supplements
days.work: Evaluate three supplement claims using FDA and NIH sources.

days.title: Trainers
days.work: Learn how to check a personal trainer's certification (NCCA-accredited).

days.title: Consumer report
days.work: Write a consumer guide to adult fitness options in your area.

objectives: Plan activity around school, work, and family

days.title: Schedules
days.work: Map a sample college or work week and find 150 minutes for activity; do a 30-minute workout.

days.title: Campus resources
days.work: Research recreation facilities and intramurals at a college or employer you're considering.

days.title: Short workouts
days.work: Design three 15-minute 'busy day' workouts and test one.

days.title: Social activity
days.work: Find a local club, league, or group activity and attend or contact it.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write about how your activity habits will change after graduation.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft a 12-week plan meeting adult guidelines (150+ min aerobic, 2 strength days).

days.title: Test week 1
days.work: Complete day 1 of your plan.

days.title: Budget
days.work: Add a budget and resource list to the plan.

days.title: Test week 1
days.work: Complete day 2 of your plan.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise the plan based on how the first days felt.

days.title: Mile
days.work: Final timed mile.

days.title: Strength
days.work: Final push-up and curl-up tests.

days.title: Flexibility
days.work: Final flexibility and resting heart rate tests.

days.title: Graph
days.work: Graph year-long data across three test points.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Write an analysis of your year's progress.

objectives: Present and defend the adult fitness plan

days.title: Finalize
days.work: Finalize the plan and do a workout from it.

days.title: Prepare
days.work: Prepare a 5-minute presentation of your plan.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the plan to family and answer questions.

days.title: Lead
days.work: Lead family through one session from your plan.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Make final revisions based on feedback.

objectives: Reflect and commit to lifelong activity

days.title: Favorite activity
days.work: Spend 45 minutes on your favorite activity from the year.

days.title: Written exam
days.work: Take the final written exam on fitness concepts and lifetime activities.

days.title: Community event
days.work: Participate in a community fun run, group hike, or open play.

days.title: Letter
days.work: Write a letter to your future self about staying active.

days.title: Celebrate
days.work: Do a celebration workout with family and log your final entry.
